header:
Date: 2025-02-25
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jared Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Rojas (Cygnus Channel Lead), Marcus Li (Cygnus CTO), Priya Singh (Cygnus SE)
Recording: Fireflies transcript export
Shared artifacts: partner-deck link (https://redwood-internal/partner-deck/cygnus), perf-spreadsheet (gdrive link pasted in chat)
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood Inference and Cygnus Compute to explore channel reseller / managed offering integration. Focus areas: integration touchpoints (VPC vs managed), entitlement and billing flows, capacity planning for GPU pools, security/compliance (SSO, KMS, audit logs), and a perf pilot. Agreed to schedule an SE deep-dive with benchmarks and to exchange NDA/MSA templates.
topics: Partner motion overview; Deployment models (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC/on-prem); Network/auth + KMS; Benchmarks and pilot framing; Commercials and margin expectations; Next steps (technical deep dive + legal).
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Maya, AE on the partner team at Redwood. Uh Jared is our solutions engineer. How are you folks?
[00:12] Elena Rojas: Hey Maya, thanks. I'm Elena, channel at Cygnus, here with Marcus and Priya. Excited to chat.
[00:18] Marcus Li: Hey all. Sorry I'm a bit early, juggling another call, but I'm here.
[00:24] Maya Chen: No problem. Quick agenda — we wanted to learn about Cygnus' GTM and typical customer workloads, share a quick overview of Redwood's deployment modes, and surface the integration touchpoints. Then if it looks good we'll plan an SE benchmark call. Sound ok?
[00:38] Priya Singh: Yep that works.
[00:41] Jared Patel: I'll also want to capture perf expectations — like is this low-latency inference at 20qps or batch-oriented embeddings.
[00:49] Elena Rojas: Our primary interest is channel/reseller partnerships. Cygnus runs a managed offering for telco edge customers and also a cloud reseller SKU. We want a partner that can give us predictable performance for coop customers and a clear margin model.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Great. To give a super fast orientation — Redwood has three main modes: Hosted API (fastest to go live), Dedicated GPU pools (reserved capacity for partners), and Private/VPC or on-prem for regulated customers. All share the same API and operational console.
[01:23] Marcus Li: When you say "dedicated pools" — do you mean we can reserve a set of GPUs and guarantee latency SLAs? How do autoscaling and burst work?
[01:34] Jared Patel: Right — dedicated is reserved capacity that you can commit to with autoscaling policies. There is a burst tier for short spikes. The runtime does continuous batching and KV cache so effective throughput is higher. For SLAs we offer latency SLOs depending on committed capacity.
[01:49] Marcus Li: Okay, and networking — for our telco customers we need VPC peering and strict egress controls and customer-managed KMS. Does Redwood support SAML SSO and bring-your-own-KMS?
[02:02] Maya Chen: Yes on both. Private deployments support customer KMS/HSM integration and we support SSO/SAML and RBAC. Audit logs and per-token tracing show up in the Console. For hosted we have a VPC option for selected partners.
[02:15] Priya Singh: How is data residency handled? Some customers need logs not to leave region.
[02:20] Jared Patel: We can pin regions for hosted and Dedicated. Private on-prem obviously keeps data local. There are options to scrub user data from metrics, and audit logs can be exported to your SIEM.
[02:30] Elena Rojas: One challenge for us is margins — partners need a clear reseller pricing model. Do you have partner tiers?
[02:37] Maya Chen: We do. Channel partners can get a partner discount off hosted usage or buy committed Dedicated pools with partner margin baked in. We'll share a partner pricing matrix — high level now, but we'll follow up with exact bands.
[02:50] Marcus Li: From a technical point, we want to run a validation pilot: run a small fleet for real telco workloads, measure p50/p95 latency and token cost, and test failover behavior. How do we run benchmarks against your runtime?
[03:03] Jared Patel: We have a benchmark harness we can share — it can run classification, chat, and streaming workloads. It supports pinned model versions and quantization profiles. We'll also provide guidance on kernel selection and sequencing. For the pilot we usually do a two-week run against a representative workload.
[03:20] Priya Singh: Is the harness public? Or do we get a repo?
[03:23] Jared Patel: We'll provide a private repo + script and a sample spreadsheet for results. We can also run a lab-run to demonstrate baseline numbers.
[03:31] Elena Rojas: Are there model compatibility constraints? Our customers sometimes want to swap models or use open weights.
[03:36] Maya Chen: Redwood supports many open models as well as curated variants. The runtime handles quantization-friendly paths. If you need special model onboarding we can do that — it's common for partners to request a certified model profile.
[03:48] Marcus Li: A bit of a naive question — what happens if a model requires more VRAM than the pool? Do you do dynamic spill or fallbacks?
[03:55] Jared Patel: Good question. We do automatic fallback to compatible model variants and have routing policies. For large models we suggest specific instance types or sharded execution. There's also prefix caching to reduce repeated compute.
[04:10] Elena Rojas: On compliance, our procurement asks for SOC 2, ISO27001, and support for customer-specific audit logs. Do you have certs?
[04:18] Maya Chen: Yes we provide SOC 2 Type II and are working on ISO readiness; we'll share our security pack. We also support per-customer audit logs and can point to our logging exports and retention controls.
[04:31] Marcus Li: For the integration, we'd like to surface a few specific items: 1) How billing flows if we resell — do you invoice Cygnus or the end customers? 2) How are entitlements provisioned programmatically? 3) How to do SSO mapping for tenant admins?
[04:47] Maya Chen: High level: we support both direct billing to partners or white-label invoicing. Entitlements are via APIs and console, with role-based access control and SAML mappings for tenant groups. We'll include an integration checklist that maps these out.
[05:02] Priya Singh: For autoscaling and burst — what controls do we have to avoid cost surprises?
[05:07] Jared Patel: You can set hard caps on burst and autoscale thresholds, and Redwood Console provides per-route cost breakdowns and token-level visibility. We also recommend caching and batching profiles to reduce per-token spend.
[05:20] Elena Rojas: Any concerns with multitenancy? We want strong isolation between different telco customers hosted on the same Dedicated pool.
[05:27] Jared Patel: Dedicated pools give you tenant isolation at the pool level; we also support per-tenant namespaces and network segmentation on Private. For strictest isolation we recommend private deployments.
[05:39] Maya Chen: Quick question for Marcus — what's the priority between latency SLO and cost for Cygnus' customers? Is it cost sensitive or latency-sensitive?
[05:45] Marcus Li: For telco edge customers it's latency-sensitive, especially for call-center and real-time transcription. But for other verticals — like batch anonymization — cost matters more. We need a flexible stack.
[05:58] Maya Chen: Makes sense. For latency scenarios we typically advise Dedicated pools with low-sequence kernels and lower batching to meet p95 targets; for batch workloads you can use hosted with aggressive batching and higher quantization.
[06:12] Elena Rojas: Are there any examples of partner success? A short case study would help our GTM.
[06:16] Maya Chen: Yep, we'll send a 1-pager for a partner that runs an edge reseller offering — anonymized but with numbers on latency and cost improvements after adopting Dedicated + cache.
[06:26] Priya Singh: On the tech side, I'd like a quick deep-dive on network setup — peering, NAT, and route reflectors we might need for telco networks. Can Jared do that?
[06:35] Jared Patel: Absolutely. I'll prep a network setup doc and we can walk it in the SE session.
[06:40] Elena Rojas: One thing we run into is customer procurement wanting clear SLAs tied to credits or refunds. How rigid are your SLAs for partners?
[06:48] Maya Chen: We have SLA tiers for Dedicated, and we can include partner-friendly terms in enterprise contracts. We'll put a summary in the partner pack and legal can iterate on MSA addenda.
[06:58] Marcus Li: For pilot sizing, what telemetry do we get? Metrics for per-route p50/p95, token counts, GPU utilization?
[07:05] Jared Patel: Yes all of those. The Console surfaces p50/p95, token usage, per-request traces, and GPU level metrics. We can also export raw telemetry to your monitoring.
[07:15] Elena Rojas: Ok, let's talk schedule. We want the SE deep-dive next week if possible. Monday or Tuesday mornings PST?
[07:22] Maya Chen: I can do Monday morning. Jared — you free Monday 9am?
[07:26] Jared Patel: Monday 9am PST works. I'll propose calendar invite and include the benchmark harness link.
[07:31] Priya Singh: Perfect. For legal, we'll have our counsel send initial NDA tonight.
[07:35] Maya Chen: Great — we'll countersign and send the partner deck and integration checklist after.
[07:40] Elena Rojas: A few small clarifications: 1) do you support reseller branding on console? 2) Is there a hosted white-label option?
[07:47] Maya Chen: We have limited white-labeling for partners — partner portal branding and API keys tied to partner. Full white-label console is available on private deployments. We'll add that to the pack.
[07:58] Marcus Li: On the model side, is there any vendor lock in for kernel/quantization stacks? If our customers want to switch quantization libs, any issues?
[08:07] Jared Patel: We try to be agnostic; the runtime supports multiple quantization backends but certified profiles are recommended. Swapping libs can work but may require re-cert.
[08:18] Elena Rojas: Cool. Anything else from Redwood?
[08:21] Maya Chen: Not from me. We'll follow up with: partner deck, security pack, benchmark harness, calendar invite for SE deep-dive.
[08:28] Priya Singh: Thanks all.
[08:29] Marcus Li: Thanks, good intro.
[08:30] Elena Rojas: Thanks Maya, Jared. Looking forward to the deep dive.
[08:33] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. I'll send notes and action items. Bye.
[08:36] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: minor transcription errors observed: "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cash", occasional dropped hyphens in model names, and speaker overlaps around 07:20-07:30.
